key_insight: PEACE improves adult-to-pediatric ECG transfer by aligning ECG signals with label-conditioned, axis-specific clinical knowledge instead of relying on global multimodal matching.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical pretraining and fine-tuning strategy for low-label pediatric ECG deployment, especially when inference must run on ECG signals alone.
method: Uses label query network (LQN) to cross-attend diagnostic labels over ECG tokens and knowledge axis tokens.
Builds positive-label-only rhythm, morphology, and ST-T descriptors for each record and aligns them with ECG features via label set aware bidirectional contrastive learning (LSBC).
Applies curriculum adaptive fusion (CAF) to gradually strengthen alignment supervision during training.
evidence_signal: On ZZU-pECG, PEACE achieved macro-average AUCs of 59.39% zero-shot, 81.74% with 50-shot, and 91.56% with full fine-tuning, and reached 96.90% macro-average AUC on PTB-XL after fine-tuning.
watch_item: Because the knowledge branch is training-only and gains depend on label-conditioned alignment, performance may be sensitive to label quality, diagnosis harmonization, and shifts in pediatric label availability.
paper_title: Knowledge-Guided Cross-Modal Fusion for Adult-to-Pediatric ECG Transfer via Label-Conditioned Contrastive Alignment
